title: Competition in Aedes aegypti larvae: effects of food distribution over time
author: Kurt Steinwascher
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bddhi236
materials: Day zero is the day the experiment begins.
Continue until all larvae have pupated or died.

steps.title: Obtain eggs and hatch
steps.instruction: Collect Aedes aegypti eggs from a colony after feeding females on a mouse, then immerse the eggs in distilled water for at least 2 hours to hatch.

steps.title: Label test tubes (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Label 160 disposable round‑bottomed test tubes (25 mm × 150 mm) with a random number and the assigned treatment.

steps.title: Fill test tubes with water
steps.instruction: On day 0 add 20 ml distilled water to each of the 160 test tubes.

steps.title: Prepare yeast stock (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Weigh baker’s yeast and dissolve in distilled water to make three stock concentrations: 8 mg ml⁻¹, 16 mg ml⁻¹ and 32 mg ml⁻¹. Ensure the yeast is completely dissolved with no residue.

steps.title: Add initial food (Day 0)
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 ml of the appropriate yeast suspension to each test tube according to its treatment:

substeps.instruction: Treatments 3, 4, 7, 8 → 0.5 ml of 8 mg ml⁻¹ (4 mg food)
Treatments 1, 2, 5, 6, 11, 12, 15, 16 → 0.5 ml of 16 mg ml⁻¹ (8 mg food)
Treatments 9, 10, 13, 14 → 0.5 ml of 32 mg ml⁻¹ (16 mg food)

steps.title: Add larvae (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Count either 4 or 8 larvae and place them into each test tube according to the density indicated on the tube label.

steps.title: Arrange and cover tubes
steps.instruction: Randomize the test tubes by their numbers, place them in a rack, and cover with cheesecloth to prevent entry of food particles or other mosquitoes.

steps.title: Store at ambient temperature
steps.instruction: Keep the test tubes in a room with ambient Florida temperatures ranging from 18 °C to 33 °C.

steps.title: Day 1 feeding (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh yeast suspensions (8 mg ml⁻¹ and 16 mg ml⁻¹). Add 0.5 ml of 8 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 3 and 7; add 0.5 ml of 16 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 11 and 15.

steps.title: Day 2 feeding (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh yeast suspensions (8 mg ml⁻¹ and 16 mg ml⁻¹). Add 0.5 ml of 8 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 3, 4, 7, 8; add 0.5 ml of 16 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 11, 12, 15, 16.

steps.title: Day 3 feeding (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh yeast suspensions (8 mg ml⁻¹, 16 mg ml⁻¹, 32 mg ml⁻¹). Add 0.5 ml of 8 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 3 and 7; 0.5 ml of 16 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 1, 5, 11, 15; 0.5 ml of 32 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 9 and 13.

steps.title: Day 4 feeding (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh yeast suspensions (8 mg ml⁻¹ and 16 mg ml⁻¹). Add 0.5 ml of 8 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 4 and 8; add 0.5 ml of 16 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 12 and 16.

steps.title: Day 5 – no food
steps.instruction: Do not add any yeast suspension to any test tube on day 5.

steps.title: Day 6 feeding (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh yeast suspensions (8 mg ml⁻¹, 16 mg ml⁻¹, 32 mg ml⁻¹). Add 0.5 ml of 8 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 4 and 8; 0.5 ml of 16 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 2, 6, 12, 16; 0.5 ml of 32 mg ml⁻¹ to treatments 10 and 14.

steps.title: Check for pupae (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Beginning on day 4, inspect each test tube for pupae. Remove any pupae before the next food addition.

steps.title: Transfer pupae to holding vials
steps.instruction: Using a fire‑polished wide‑mouth glass pipette (~2 mm diameter), pick each pupa from its test tube, place it into a numbered holding shell vial containing 10 ml distilled water, and record the original tube number, treatment, and date. One pupa per holding vial.

steps.title: Weigh, sex, and return pupae
steps.instruction: Remove the pupa from the holding vial with a pipette, blot on paper towel, weigh to the nearest 0.01 mg, record weight, determine sex under a 10× stereomicroscope, record sex, then return the pupa to its water vial to complete pupation.

steps.title: Obtain eggs and hatch (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Collect Aedes aegypti eggs from a colony after mouse‑fed females and immerse in distilled water for at least 2 hours to hatch.

steps.title: Label shell vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Label 60 flat‑bottomed shell vials (25 mm × 95 mm) with a random number and the assigned treatment.

steps.title: Fill vials with water
steps.instruction: Add 20 ml distilled water to each of the 60 vials.

steps.title: Prepare yeast for each treatment
steps.instruction: Weigh baker’s yeast and dissolve in distilled water to achieve the required food per larva (2, 3, 4, 5 mg larva⁻¹) for the three densities (1, 2, 3 larvae vial⁻¹). For example, 2 mg larva⁻¹ × 1 larva = 2 mg yeast in 0.5 ml water; 5 mg larva⁻¹ × 3 larvae = 15 mg yeast in 0.5 ml water. Add the calculated total yeast to the 20 ml water in each vial (5 replicates per treatment).

steps.title: Add larvae (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Count 1, 2 or 3 larvae and place them into each vial according to its treatment label.

steps.title: Arrange and cover vials
steps.instruction: Randomize the vials by number, place them in a rack, and cover with cheesecloth.

steps.title: Store at ambient temperature (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Keep the vials in a room with ambient Florida temperatures ranging from 18 °C to 33 °C.

steps.title: Check for pupae (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Starting on day 4, examine each vial for pupae and remove any before further handling.

steps.title: Transfer pupae to holding vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Using a fire‑polished wide‑mouth glass pipette (~2 mm), move each pupa to a numbered holding vial with 10 ml distilled water, recording tube number, treatment, and date; one pupa per vial.

steps.title: Weigh, sex, and return pupae (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Blot each pupa, weigh to 0.01 mg, record weight, determine sex under a 10× stereomicroscope, record sex, then return the pupa to water to finish development.

steps.title: Obtain eggs and hatch (Exp 3)
steps.instruction: Collect Aedes aegypti eggs from a colony after mouse‑fed females and immerse in distilled water for at least 2 hours to hatch.

steps.title: Label test tubes (Exp 3)
steps.instruction: Label 150 disposable round‑bottomed test tubes (25 mm × 150 mm) with a random number and the assigned treatment.

steps.title: Fill test tubes with water
steps.instruction: Add 20 ml distilled water to each of the 150 test tubes.

steps.title: Add first food input (Day 0)
steps.instruction: Weigh baker’s yeast and dissolve to deliver 1 mg yeast in 0.5 ml distilled water; add 0.5 ml of this suspension (1 mg food) to every test tube.

steps.title: Add one larva per tube
steps.instruction: Place a single larva into each of the 150 test tubes.

steps.title: Arrange and cover tubes (Exp 3)
steps.instruction: Randomize the tubes by number, place them in a rack, and cover with cheesecloth.

steps.title: Store at ambient temperature (Exp 3)
steps.instruction: Keep the tubes in a room with ambient Florida temperatures ranging from 18 °C to 33 °C.

steps.title: Day 6 second food addition
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh yeast suspensions of 2 mg ml⁻¹, 4 mg ml⁻¹ and 6 mg ml⁻¹. Add 0.5 ml of 2 mg ml⁻¹ to treatment 1, 0.5 ml of 4 mg ml⁻¹ to treatment 2, and 0.5 ml of 6 mg ml⁻¹ to treatment 3.

steps.title: Day 8 second food addition
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh yeast suspensions of 2 mg ml⁻¹, 4 mg ml⁻¹ and 6 mg ml⁻¹. Add 0.5 ml of 2 mg ml⁻¹ to treatment 4, 0.5 ml of 4 mg ml⁻¹ to treatment 5, and 0.5 ml of 6 mg ml⁻¹ to treatment 6.

steps.title: Check for pupae (Exp 3)
steps.instruction: Beginning on day 4, inspect each test tube for pupae and remove any before the next food addition.

steps.title: Transfer pupae to holding vials (Exp 3)
steps.instruction: Using a fire‑polished wide‑mouth glass pipette (~2 mm), move each pupa to a numbered holding vial containing 10 ml distilled water, recording tube number, treatment, and date; one pupa per vial.

steps.title: Weigh, sex, and return pupae (Exp 3)
steps.instruction: Blot each pupa, weigh to the nearest 0.01 mg, record weight, determine sex under a 10× stereomicroscope, record sex, then return the pupa to water to complete pupation.
